tailMarker.anomalyNote: The marker is a PRESERVATIVE at rank 18, one rank ahead of Parfum @19, in a 21-entry list. That gives the cohort's second-longest above-tail segment and demotes almost nothing — only Parfum and its two declared allergens sit in the tail. No §3.1 anomaly. Consequence worth noting: a Naturkosmetik formula with a short preservative system and a short fragrance block gets nearly its whole list credited, while conventional formulas with early Parfum lose theirs. The tail rule is not weight-neutral across formulation philosophies (AP-08-NATURKOSMETIK).  ||  PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1, added under v0.2): PLAUSIBLE. Seventeen above-tail entries carry the entire architecture (CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, DISTEAROYLETHYL DIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4, BEHENYL ALCOHOL @5, the protein block @7/@8/@9, the humectant cluster @3/@6/@12/@13/@14) and all outrank POTASSIUM SORBATE @18; conventional O/W emulsion. Neither limb fires. HELIANTHUS ANNUUS SEED OIL @17 is the tail_index - 1 species and is excluded from carrying a structural signal (R3) - it is the formula's only lipid, so S3 fails either way.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Formula-only, brand-direct DE INCI of record (sha256 0e174314…), above-tail ranks 1–17; category-relative to the German drugstore rinse-out mask shelf.
conditioningLevel.rationale: Exactly one §9.1 structural signal is satisfied. The formula carries a broad and genuinely material payload — three proteins, five humectants — but §9.1 measures structural conditioning intensity, not payload breadth, and on that axis this is a single-cationic, single-lipid formula. E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential, not measured treatment performance.
evidenceSignals: CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — long-chain fatty alcohol in the top three, the one satisfied signal
DISTEAROYLETHYL DIMONIUM CHLORIDE (rank 4) — the only cationic surfactant at any rank
BEHENYL ALCOHOL (rank 5) — a second fatty alcohol; fatty-alcohol breadth is not a §9.1 signal and is excluded from S3 by definition
HELIANTHUS ANNUUS SEED OIL (rank 17) — the only non-fatty-alcohol lipid above the tail; S3 needs two
conditioningLevel.derivation: S1 = NOT satisfied (one cationic species). S2 = satisfied (Cetearyl Alcohol @2). S3 = NOT satisfied (one lipid, against a required two; the two fatty alcohols are excluded from the lipid count by S3's own wording). Count = 1 of 3.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moderate`: §9.1's 'everything else, including exactly one satisfied signal'.

`high` does not apply: it requires ≥2 signals, and only S2 holds. The formula's most distinctive features — the three-protein cluster and the five-member humectant cluster — are invisible to §9.1 by design, because D1 confines this field to structural position and assigns protein to repair_support_level and humectants to the focus layer.
`low` does not apply: Cetearyl Alcohol @2 defeats its second conjunct.
Confidence `moderate` by §9.1's own rule: high confidence requires ≥2 signals pointing the same way.

Re-derived under v0.2 (R3): the value `moderate` STANDS. S1 fails — DISTEAROYLETHYL DIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4 is the only cationic surfactant above the tail. S2 is satisfied by CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2 (BEHENYL ALCOHOL @5 is a second long-chain fatty alcohol but S2 reads rank, not breadth). S3 fails on the tail-edge exclusion: HELIANTHUS ANNUUS SEED OIL @17 is the formula's only lipid and is exactly the tail_index − 1 species, so it cannot carry a signal — and one lipid would not satisfy S3 in any case. One signal; S1 absent. No material counter-signal fires.
counterSignals: Payload breadth versus structural narrowness: this is the cohort's clearest case where the two diverge, and §9.1 correctly reports the structural reading. Recorded so the divergence is visible to the review rather than silently absorbed.
Behenyl Alcohol @5 is a C22 fatty alcohol and a real emollient load; §9.1 gives fatty-alcohol breadth no credit beyond the S2 rank test.
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support.
Downstream cost: conditioning_level `moderate` caps damage_fit at healthy + moderately_damaged even though a specialist protein route exists — see the damageFit record and AP-08-SPECIALISTGATE.

careDirection.evidenceScope: Formula-only, above-tail ranks 1–17; comparative care emphasis, never an assertion about a user's protein or moisture state (G6).
careDirection.rationale: This is the cohort's only genuinely substantive `balanced`: three distinct hydrolyzed proteins at consecutive ranks 7–9 satisfy the material R5 route on both of its legs, and five distinct qualifying humectants above the tail satisfy the humectant-cluster leg of the balanced test — not the loose S3 lipid leg that carried #04 and #05. Both sides of the value are real. E2 ceiling: comparative emphasis, not a delivered outcome.
evidenceSignals: HYDROLYZED CORN PROTEIN (7), HYDROLYZED WHEAT PROTEIN (8), HYDROLYZED SOY PROTEIN (9) — three distinct qualifying R5 species above the tail, at consecutive ranks

GLYCERIN (3), BETAINE (6), SODIUM LACTATE (12), SODIUM HYALURONATE (13), ALOE BARBADENSIS LEAF JUICE POWDER (14) — five distinct qualifying humectant-class members above the tail, four of them non-glycerin
ARGININE (rank 11) — free amino acid, deliberately EXCLUDED from the humectant cluster (not on R9's list) and excluded from R5 by the mask delta
HELIANTHUS ANNUUS SEED OIL (17) — the single lipid; S3 is NOT satisfied, so the lipid leg of the balanced test is unavailable here

LACTIC ACID (10) / SODIUM LACTATE (12) — a buffer pair; C3's amidoamine-neutraliser reading does NOT apply because the cationic is a permanent esterquat, so Sodium Lactate is counted as a humectant on its own merits
careDirection.derivation: §9.3 material-R5 test satisfied on leg (a) (three distinct species above the tail) and independently on leg (b) (a qualifying species at above-tail rank 7, inside the first eight). Then the `balanced` test: material R5 route AND (a qualifying humectant cluster of ≥3 distinct humectants above the tail with ≥2 non-glycerin, OR S3). The humectant cluster leg succeeds with five members and four non-glycerin; the S3 leg fails with one lipid. → `balanced`, earned on the humectant leg.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `balanced`: both conjuncts hold, and the second holds on the strict humectant-cluster leg rather than the loose lipid leg. D6 reserves `balanced` for a substantive mixed protein-plus-moisture architecture; three proteins and five humectants above the tail is that architecture.
`protein` does not apply: the humectant leg is substantive and independent, so this is not a protein-dominant formula.
`moisture` does not apply: three hydrolyzed proteins at ranks 7–9 is a dominant protein-film route by any reading, and `moisture` is defined as the coherent direction WITHOUT one.

Aloe counted once and never as a strong member, per lexicon family 7's 'reconstituted powder at trace level' caution — the source list says 'Leaf Juice Powder' explicitly. Even discounting Aloe entirely, the cluster is four members with three non-glycerin and still clears.

Re-checked under v0.2 (R6). The value is unchanged and its reading is now recorded explicitly: `balanced_reading: both_substantive`. Both legs are substantive above the tail — a material R5 route (HYDROLYZED CORN @7, WHEAT @8, SOY @9) AND a qualifying humectant cluster meeting §9.5.3 criterion 1 (GLYCERIN @3, BETAINE @6, SODIUM LACTATE @12, SODIUM HYALURONATE @13, ALOE @14: five distinct, four non-glycerin). R6 deletes the lipid-leg path into `balanced`, which is what moves #04 and #05 to `protein`; this product never used that path and is unaffected. Reading (b) is unavailable at clause 1 (a protein anchor is present).
counterSignals: D4 heavy-protein-payload counter-signal FIRES (three distinct R5 species above the tail), binding confidence to `moderate` (§13 effect 2). Confidence would otherwise have been `high` — resolved tail marker, brand-direct verbatim source, unambiguous route separation.

Arginine's exclusion is a judgment: lexicon family 5b allows free amino acids 'at most a very weak contribution to the humectant cluster when several appear above the tail with no plausible neutraliser role', and here there IS no amidoamine to neutralise. I excluded it because R9's enumeration does not list it. Including it would raise the cluster to six and change nothing.
limitations: INCI discloses no molecular weight; P-5's mechanics evidence is entirely MW-conditional, so the three-protein cluster supports 'a protein film route is present' and nothing about strength or breakage.

Banned vocabulary observed: no 'protein overload' language, and no 'hygral fatigue' reading of the humectant cluster (lexicon family 7: an unestablished construct that must never appear as a rule, a warning, or copy).

exact-product positioning used as the tie-breaker, verbatim: product name 'Intense Hydration'; claims 'Feuchtigkeitsbooster für trockenes Haar', 'schützt langanhaltend vor dem Austrocknen'. The competing claim leg ('3-Fach Protein Komplex') is recorded as the losing candidate's corroboration
primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: the protein cluster is one M2 observation and the humectant cluster one M5 observation — genuinely disjoint, and neither is M1. Step 3: `repair` clears its protein-film disjunct. Step 4: `moisture` independently clears all four §9.5.3 criteria, including criterion 2 in both its baseline sentence and its R5 lipid-led limbs. Both candidates therefore cleared their own thresholds on the formula, which is the definition of `dual_supported`. §9.5.1 as scoped by R7 then breaks the tie on exact-product positioning: `moisture` primary, `repair` secondary.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moisture` as primary: a formula-supported candidate, chosen over an equally formula-supported candidate by exact-product positioning on a genuinely `dual_supported` verdict. R7's discipline observed exhaustively — the claim chose between two candidates the formula already supports; it created no third candidate, lowered no threshold, upgraded no `nonspecific` evidence, and substituted for no corroboration leg.

`repair` does not take the primary slot — the change from v0.1. Under v0.1 the §9.5.2 step order alone decided it, and the claim leg had nothing to do; R7 states that the order decides which routes are tested first, not which of two cleared routes wins. `repair` keeps a secondary slot, so both endpoints remain on the record.

§9.5.3 criterion 3 is satisfied in the direction that matters here: no RICHER special-purpose route wins. `repair` cleared, but the tie-break assigned it the secondary slot, and criterion 3's own text contemplates exactly this pairing.

R5's lipid-led disqualifier was tested and does NOT fire: one R4a mid-band oil at rank 17, no R4b heavy lipid above the marker. This formula is the opposite of lipid-led — it is the cohort's leanest humectant-forward architecture after #09.
`smoothing` does not apply: its claim ('glättet die Haarstruktur & wirkt Frizz entgegen') has no architecture behind it — no silicone, no substantive polymer, one lipid at rank 17.
`general` does not apply: two differentiators cleared.
counterSignals: Confidence stays `moderate`: §9.5.3's confidence rule requires 'no competing route' for `high`, and `repair` is a live competing route sitting in the secondary slot.

'verbessert die Kämmbarkeit ohne zu beschweren' is a lightness claim. It is recorded and creates nothing: `weight_potential` is `moderate`, so no §9.2 conflict arises and `weight_high_conflict` does not fire.

The tie-break is claim-dependent by construction. A reviewer who read the verdict as `repair_supported` rather than `dual_supported` would not reach the tie-break at all — but the cluster's independent clearance of all four D5 criteria is what makes the verdict dual, and that is a formula finding.
limitations: Wording rule (D5, binding) observed absolutely: this record says 'humectant-forward comparative direction' and never 'hydrates', 'proven hydration', 'moisturizes' or 'restores moisture balance' — notwithstanding that the product's own name is 'Intense Hydration'.
Adapter boundary: `moisture` has no `functional_benefits` counterpart and reaches production only via `balance_direction`. No projection is authorized here.

focusCareVerdict.note: Unchanged verdict, resolved tie (R7, 2026-09-14). The formula genuinely supports both directions: three distinct hydrolyzed proteins at ranks 7–9 (M2) and five distinct humectants across four families above the tail (M5), on disjoint mechanisms with almost no M1 richness to confuse either with. This is the cohort's only `dual_supported` verdict. Under v0.1 the claim leg was recorded as eligible but NOT applied, because §9.5.2's step order had already resolved the primary slot to `repair`; AP-08-TIEBREAK escalated the conflict. R7 settles it: the step order decides which routes are tested first, not which of two cleared routes wins, and on a genuinely dual verdict exact-product positioning may break the tie at any step and in either direction, including which candidate takes primary and which takes a secondary slot. Claim text applied as tie-breaker, verbatim: product name 'Intense Hydration'; claim 'Feuchtigkeitsbooster für trockenes Haar'. Competing focus that lost the primary slot: `repair`, which retains the secondary slot.
